Text.text: You are an operations assistant completing a task with the available tools. Work autonomously and never ask the user questions. Be efficient: keep the number of steps as low as you can. When the task is complete, call the `submit_result` tool exactly once with the JSON shape requested in the task, then stop.

Schedule a 60-minute meeting for the whole team (everyone returned by list_users) during the week of 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-19. Constraints: the slot must lie entirely within working hours 09:00-17:00 UTC, must start on a 30-minute boundary, and every team member must be free for the full hour. Find the EARLIEST such slot in the week. When done, submit {"start": .., "end": ..} as ISO-8601 UTC timestamps via submit_result.

Reasoning.summary:
Let me start by listing users and getting their availability for the week. I'll use the compose tool to do everything in one shot: list users, fetch availability for each user for each day, compute the earliest 60-minute slot within 09:00-17:00 UTC starting on a 30-min boundary where everyone is free.

Let me write a Lua script.

Days: 2026-06-15 (Monday) through 2026-06-19 (Friday).

For each day in order, for each candidate start time (09:00, 09:30, ..., 16:00), check if [start, start+60min) intersects any busy interval of any user. Busy intervals are {start="HH:MM", end="HH:MM"} UTC. If no overlap for all users, that's the slot.

Overlap condition: busy.start < slotEnd && slotStart < busy.end.

Times are strings "HH:MM" — can compare lexicographically since same format.

Return the answer and also submit it? I need to call submit_result exactly once. I can call it inside compose via tool('submit_result', ...). Then also return the result. That would be efficient — one compose call total.

Let me write the script.

input.script:
local users = tool('list_users', {})
local days = {"2026-06-15","2026-06-16","2026-06-17","2026-06-18","2026-06-19"}

local function toMin(hhmm)
  local h, m = hhmm:match("(%d+):(%d+)")
  return tonumber(h) * 60 + tonumber(m)
end

local function toHHMM(mins)
  return string.format("%02d:%02d", math.floor(mins / 60), mins % 60)
end

-- gather busy intervals per user per day
local busy = {}
for _, d in ipairs(days) do
  busy[d] = {}
  for _, u in ipairs(users) do
    local r = tool('get_availability', { user_id = u.id, date = d })
    for _, b in ipairs(r.busy or {}) do
      busy[d][#busy[d] + 1] = { s = toMin(b.start), e = toMin(b.end), who = u.id }
    end
  end
end

local found = nil
for _, d in ipairs(days) do
  for start = 9 * 60, 16 * 60, 30 do
    local finish = start + 60
    local ok = true
    for _, b in ipairs(busy[d]) do
      if b.s < finish and start < b.e then ok = false break end
    end
    if ok then
      found = { date = d, s = start, e = finish }
      break
    end
  end
  if found then break end
end

if not found then return { error = "no slot found" } end

local answer = {
  start = found.date .. "T" .. toHHMM(found.s) .. ":00Z",
  ["end"] = found.date .. "T" .. toHHMM(found.e) .. ":00Z",
}
local sub = tool('submit_result', { answer = answer })
return { answer = answer, submitted = sub, user_count = #users }
